summary: Seal backup SMB3 and VM-storage SMB mount credentials with systemd-creds so mount units decrypt them at mount time, including boot. API impact: none; Core-internal mount handling.

guide.reason: SMB3 repositories now remount after a reboot and sealed passwords are host-bound.

api.reason: No Controller-Core contract changed; only how Core stores and loads an SMB password locally.

roadmap.reason: Fixes a regression in the existing destination candidate.

state.record: systemd-creds sealed file per receipt or credential reference under the Core state directory, referenced by the generated mount unit. A fresh Controller holds nothing; Core reports receipts as before.
state.reason: The secret and its mount unit stay on the host that mounts the share.

verification.method: Focused Go tests with a fake systemd-creds runner: unit content, no plaintext at rest, seal and decrypt failures, and refusal of the real tool under test.
verification.limits: Real systemd-creds with TPM2 or the host key, and remount after a real reboot, were not run; they need a real host.
